elements.element: Customer is not subject to any non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 states that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, and expressly confirms that Customer has made no non-compete commitment. Section 12.4 now permits, rather than prohibits, competing activities.

elements.element: Customer is not subject to any field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory and to develop, acquire, license, sell, or use any product or service.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction is limited to one specifically named competing product.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction remains operative, so the condition requiring a named-product limitation is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction applies only during the agreement term.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction remains operative. Although Section 12.4 refers to the term and 24 months thereafter, it grants permission during that period rather than imposing a restriction, while Section 12.3 broadly confirms no restriction.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction may not last more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction remains operative, so there is no restrictive duration exceeding 12 months. The 24-month language qualifies an affirmative permission, not a prohibition.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction excludes Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly states that nothing restricts Customer from developing any product or service, and Section 12.4 also affirmatively permits development of competing products or services.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction excludes acquisitions by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly states that nothing restricts Customer from acquiring any product or service, and Section 12.4 also affirmatively permits acquisitions of competing products or services.

result.reason: The operative redline eliminates the non-compete by changing the prohibition in Section 12.4 into an affirmative permission, consistent with the comprehensive freedom-of-operation language in Section 12.3. It therefore reaches the preferred position, and the conditional fallback limitations are also satisfied because no restriction remains. The edit is minimal and does not alter unrelated commercial terms. Drafting quality is slightly reduced by retaining the unnecessary term-plus-24-month qualifier on an affirmative permission, which is awkward and potentially invites implication arguments, though Section 12.3 resolves the operative effect.
